description:
## Finding

`ValidationPolicy` at `pkix-path/src/lib.rs:516` has 5 `bool` fields:

```
enforce_key_usage: bool
initial_explicit_policy: bool
initial_any_policy_inhibit: bool
initial_policy_mapping_inhibit: bool
require_subject_alt_name: bool
require_rfc822_san: bool   // 6th!
```

Actually 6 if you count `require_rfc822_san`. Clippy's `clippy::struct_excessive_bools` (default threshold 3) flags this.

## Why it matters

`ValidationPolicy { enforce_key_usage: true, initial_explicit_policy: false, initial_any_policy_inhibit: false, initial_policy_mapping_inhibit: false, ...}` is hard to read at a callsite and easy to typo. The fields are also semantically related — three of them (`initial_*_policy*`) are RFC 5280 §6.1.1 inputs that travel together, and two (`require_subject_alt_name`, `require_rfc822_san`) gate one another (the rfc822 flag has no effect unless the SAN flag is set, per docs).

## Suggestion

Two clusters could be enums:

```rust
pub enum PolicyMode {
    None,                       // initial_explicit_policy=false, etc
    RequireExplicit,
    InhibitAnyPolicy,
    InhibitPolicyMapping,
    // or a bitflag-style PolicyFlags
}

pub enum SanRequirement {
    None,
    Required,
    RequireRfc822,              // implies Required
}
```

This is opinion-territory — the current shape is RFC-faithful. P3 because the dependency between `require_subject_alt_name` and `require_rfc822_san` is a real footgun that the type system could enforce.

## Priority

P3 — opinion. Not a bug; a hardening idiom.
title: P3: ValidationPolicy has 6 bool fields; require_rfc822_san depends on require_subject_alt_name without type-system enforcement
